weakness: The program looked for a placement spot only in a fixed preferred area of the table. When movable clutter filled that area it fell back to the least-bad spot, or to spots under an overhanging cabinet. It moved the held 22 cm box along free planner paths, which ignore the held object, so the box was swept through the clutter and knocked out of the grasp or tilted. When a descent stopped short, it opened the gripper anyway and dropped the box from the air.
how_found: Questioned A9 (free table space in a fixed region): real countertops are cluttered. Screening the frozen pipeline against a table filled with eight movable boxes gave 0.2 on 5 seeds; the gate measured 0.0 on 10.
why_missed: In the base scene the preferred area was always empty, so the spot fallback, the carry path of the held object and the release-height check were never exercised.
fix: Three repairs. (1) Search spots over the whole table: clearance from every detected obstacle footprint, using world-frame extents, and nothing hanging over the spot below the object's height plus 35 cm. (2) Release only after the descent reaches resting height; otherwise back up and try the next spot. (3) Transport the held object in straight segments: leave the container towards the robot at rim height, change height in place to a band 3 cm above everything under the path and below anything over it, cross, then descend vertically.
general_rule: Treat a held object as part of the robot: route it yourself through space you have checked for its full volume (the motion planner does not see it), pick destinations by measured clearance over the whole reachable surface instead of a preferred area, and only release it once it is at its resting height.

weakness: The program assumed the box stood upright. Its grasp points sat at fixed heights above an 'upright' bottom, its fingers closed horizontally whatever the box's axis, the lift height came from the upright half-height, and the box was put down in whatever orientation it had been grasped in. A box leaning about 34 deg against the basket wall was therefore grasped off its axis or carried tilted, and it toppled when released. Its orientation estimates came from one noisy detection.
how_found: Questioned A1 (the box stands upright): items in a basket often lean against the wall. Screening showed that a box pushed towards the far side settles leaning on every seed, and the frozen pipeline scored 0.0 on 5 seeds; the gate measured 0.1 on 10.
why_missed: In the base scene the box always stood upright, so nothing depended on its orientation, and taking the orientation from a single noisy detection never mattered.
fix: Average orientation as well as position over repeated detections. Put grasp points on the box's actual long axis, with the fingers closing perpendicular to it. Compute the lift from the box's lowest point (its vertical extent), not from an upright half-height. Once the box is carried over the free spot, turn it upright in the hand by rotating the gripper about the grasp point (5 cm higher if out of reach), then lower and release.
general_rule: Measure an object's actual orientation (averaging repeated detections) instead of assuming its canonical pose; grasp relative to its real axes; and before placing it, correct its orientation in the hand, in free space the arm can reach, to the pose the goal requires.

weakness: The program left the basket straight towards the robot and relied on shallow approaches from the robot's side, the only grasps from which the arm can lift the box 13 cm over the rim. A fixed 36 cm item standing in front of the basket blocks both: the exit sweeps the held box into it, and the hand passes over it too low on a shallow approach.
how_found: Questioned A8 (the path from the container towards the robot is free): counters hold kettles and paper-towel holders in front of baskets. The frozen pipeline scored 0.0 on 5 screening seeds and 0.2 at the gate; the expert scored 0.0.
why_missed: In every earlier scene the space between the robot and the basket was empty, so the exit direction and the approach side were never choices.
fix: Six repairs, none reached 0.8 on v3 while keeping v2. (1) Exit in the first direction whose swept path is clear: v3 0.1. (2) Add an approach from the workspace-centre side, open the gripper only when needed, lift fallbacks (move towards the robot, then pitch the hand shallower), checked by detection: v3 0.7. (3) Hold checks, upright low over the spot first, retry from the current state: v3 0.6, v2 0.8. (4) Shallow elevations first across all grasp heights: 0.5. (5) A lower grasp height: 0.3. (6) Retry with the other arm: 0.5, v2 0.7. Unsolved: where the basket sits on the microwave the box has to rise above the arm's comfortable reach, the item removes the approaches that still reach that high, and the fallbacks produce motions at the reach limit (tracking errors, cabinet and table contacts, tilted boxes). The pipeline was reverted to round 2.
general_rule: Before committing to a grasp, check that the whole sequence it implies (grasp, lift high enough, exit along a clear path) stays inside the arm's comfortable reach; when obstacles remove those approaches, change the plan (another arm, another exit, first clearing the way) instead of stacking fallbacks that run the arm at its reach limit.

weakness: The program chose the destination once, before carrying the object, and lowered it there without looking again. A tray that slid onto that part of the counter during the carry was hit, so the box was set down on or against it and toppled.
how_found: Questioned A12 (nothing moves on its own): on a shared counter, other objects get pushed around while the robot works. Screening showed 0.4 on 5 seeds; the gate measured 0.4 on 10.
why_missed: Nothing in the earlier scenes moved, so an observation made before the carry was still true at the release.
fix: Right before lowering: wait until the scene is still (obstacle positions averaged over 4 detections, compared 0.5 s apart, up to 4 s); re-check the chosen spot's clearance against the current obstacles; if it is taken, choose a new free spot from the current state and carry there (up to 3 times).
general_rule: Re-observe the target area, and let moving things come to rest, immediately before an irreversible action such as a release: plans made earlier can be invalidated by the time they are executed.

weakness: The program judged its motions by the commanded positions. Under a 1.2 kg load the arm sagged 1-2 cm below the commanded height, so the lift check (TCP moved less than commanded) declared the lift incomplete and gave up, though the box had in fact cleared the rim; carry and release heights were off by the same sag.
how_found: Questioned A5/A11 (a light box; the arm reaches the commanded heights while carrying it): full cartons weigh about 1 kg. Screening a 1.2 kg carton gave 0.2 on 5 seeds; the gate measured 0.2 on 10. The trace showed the lift reporting success and the pipeline stopping right after it.
why_missed: With a 0.1 kg box the commanded and the actual heights agreed, so checking the command looked like checking the world.
fix: Closed-loop heights from detection. Lift until the measured lowest point of the box clears the rim, correcting up to 4 times; corrections are capped at 4 cm beyond the first estimate, so a box sliding in the fingers is not chased upwards (an uncapped loop asked for a height outside the workspace). Before crossing, measure the box and top up any sag. Before releasing, measure the remaining gap to the table and lower by it. Two repairs; eval --all: base 0.8, v1 1.0, v2 0.9, v4 0.8, v5 0.9.
general_rule: Judge every motion by its measured effect on the object, re-detecting after the move, not by what was commanded: loads, slip and tracking errors separate commanded from actual poses. Bound every corrective loop so it cannot chase a slipping object.
